classification.difficultyReason: Construct a square from symbolic paver dimensions, then connect the expansion of (a+3b)^2 to counts of three paver types and a valid geometric partition; the arrangement is not supplied.

content.prompt: A brick company provides rectangular and square pavers.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Draw a diagram to show how two different square pavers of side lengths $a$ and $b$ respectively, and two identical rectangular pavers with dimensions $a\times b$, can be arranged into a square.

answer.short: A square of side length $a+b$, partitioned into one $a\times a$ square, one $b\times b$ square and two $a\times b$ rectangles.
answer.worked:
Place the two rectangles beside adjacent sides of the $a\times a$ square. The $b\times b$ square fills the remaining corner.
$$\begin{align*}a^2+2ab+b^2&=(a+b)^2\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4a; answer figure on teacher PDF page 10
spec.description: Unshaded illustrative partition; a and b remain symbolic side lengths.
spec.mathematics: One a² square, one b² square and two ab rectangles form a square of side a+b.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many of each type of paver enables you to pave a square area of side length $a+3b$? Draw a diagram to illustrate how this can be done.

answer.short: 1 square paver $a\times a$, 9 square pavers $b\times b$ and 6 rectangular pavers $a\times b$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(a+3b)^2&=a^2+2\times a\times3b+(3b)^2\\(a+3b)^2&=a^2+6ab+9b^2\end{align*}$$
Use one $a\times a$ square, three $a\times b$ rectangles along each of two adjacent sides, and nine $b\times b$ squares in the remaining corner.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 4b; answer figure on teacher PDF page 10
spec.description: Unshaded paver partition with all sixteen pieces shown; diagram proportions are illustrative.
spec.mathematics: A square of side a+3b contains one a² square, six ab rectangles and nine b² squares.
